title: Stability of Brenier maps
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's proof (2026) that, for the uniform probability measure on a compact convex body in R^d, d >= 2, quadratic optimal transport maps satisfy ||T_mu - T_nu||_{L^2} <= C W_2(mu,nu)^(1/3) uniformly over all targets in a fixed compact set, and that the exponent one third is optimal, already on a cube with three-atom targets. The proof is given in full, with no named hypothesis. The first lesson treats convex bodies and the optimality of gradients of finite affine maxima, states the theorem and proves its sharpness. The second computes the derivatives of the masses and moments of Laguerre cells and constructs intercepts for prescribed masses. The third proves a uniform estimate of moment changes by mass changes, from a midpoint coupling by Knothe's rearrangement. The fourth moves the sites of finite targets with fixed masses and bounds the distance of the potentials by W_2. The fifth turns potentials into maps with a slice interpolation inequality and passes to all targets.
prerequisites: core course Measure and Integration: Lebesgue measure, image measures, Fubini and Tonelli, dominated convergence
core course Real Analysis II (Lebl, Basic Analysis II): the implicit function theorem (Theorem 8.5.6) and the Arzela-Ascoli theorem (Theorem 11.6.9)
the lessons prove every other fact they use, including the geometry of convex bodies, the Knothe rearrangement and the differentiability of convex functions

checks.reading: The manuscript 'Sharp One-Third Stability of Brenier Maps' (OpenAI, 25 Sep 2026; main.tex and six section files, 1,370 lines of TeX) was read in full on 14 Oct 2026, and every step of its argument was derived again while the lessons were written: the null boundary and sections of convex bodies; the optimality of finite affine maxima; the cube example with its masses, distances and symmetric difference; the Laguerre cell derivatives by telescoping indicators, their continuity, the distinct tie hyperplanes and the connectivity of the face graph; the prescribed masses by convex minimization and the implicit function theorem; the Knothe construction, its Jacobian and the midpoint density bound; the moment estimate with the constants 5 and 162; the cyclical monotonicity of finite optimal couplings, the distinct intermediate sites, the duality identity and the intercept speed; the endpoint limits; the cube potential distance; the gradient interpolation on slices with the constants 12 and 28; the finite stability; the approximation by nets, the limit potential and the Fenchel argument for existence and uniqueness; the main theorem. No error found. Differences of presentation, none a correction: the statement that coordinate partial derivatives of a convex function give its gradient is a separate lemma with the uniqueness of supporting slopes; the swap argument for the monotonicity of finite optimal couplings is written out; an exercise records the Fenchel argument of the last lesson for one affine maximum. Observation: in random tests on the square (lesson checks), the ratio of the two sides of the moment estimate never exceeded 0.31 R^2, far below 162 R^2; the inequality A/4 <= R^2 B/8 + (R/2) sqrt(AB) alone gives the constant (1 + sqrt(3/2))^2, about 4.95, in place of 5. Free sources read on 14 Oct 2026: the arXiv identifiers of Kitagawa-Merigot-Thibert (1603.05579) and Delalande-Merigot (2103.05934) were confirmed; the cited results are attributions and are not used. Letrouit's conjecture (C. R. Math., open access) and Knothe (Michigan Math. J.) are cited for context and method. Core course results used: the implicit function theorem (Lebl, Basic Analysis II, Theorem 8.5.6), the Arzela-Ascoli theorem (Theorem 11.6.9), and Fubini, Tonelli, dominated convergence and image measures from Measure and Integration. Their proofs were not checked again. Checked by the program plan/checks_20261014/bs_check.py (five parts: the cube example exactly and by Monte Carlo; the Laguerre cell derivative formulas against finite differences on 169 random configurations in a square, by exact polygon clipping; prescribed masses by Newton iteration, the duality identity and the moment estimate on 120 configurations; the Knothe Jacobian, the midpoint density and the constants; the gradient interpolation on random convex maxima). The first run failed one part because of an error in the check itself (a variable declared positive in a symmetric integral); after the correction all parts pass (outputs bs_check_run_20261014a.txt and b.txt).

open_obligations: No named hypothesis. The implicit function theorem and the Arzela-Ascoli theorem from the core course Real Analysis II and the measure theory of Measure and Integration are cited; their proofs were not checked again for this course.

The history in the first lesson (earlier exponents and constants; Letrouit's conjecture) is quoted from the manuscript and the cited sources and was not checked beyond the statement of the conjecture.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
